Not expected to change, named so nobody hunts for it: `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.js` fixes the corpus by directory (`CORPUS_DIRS`), so a book is in the corpus by being copied into one of the two directories; `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` reads that module and needs no edit. GOAL (increment 1 only): put `Dogs of War.cat` into `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/`, record its provenance in that directory's README, re-baseline the corpus bookkeeping the added book moves, and keep `npm test` green. The seven definitive books and the 17-file inventory re-baseline belong to increment 2 and are not touched here — `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` and its README stay exactly as they are.

MEASURED FACTS (I cloned the upstream repo into the scratchpad and ran a throwaway node script against the extraction library; see testPlan for the method). Everything below is computed, not estimated:
- Upstream `artkoenig/Warhammer-Fantasy-6th-edition` HEAD is today exactly the pinned commit `9c7203c94221a4a98d5c1ffcfcfaedafe7d6d233`.
- `Dogs of War.cat` at that commit: 304257 bytes, sha256 `90211630f9fdf6169289fe6a98d6ab84c521cc38644d2c24ca9f720a285a9e66`. Header: `<catalogue id="4887-12ed-22a2-f461" name="Dogs of War" revision="4" gameSystemId="6d8e-38d9-3c69-febf" gameSystemRevision="8">`, i.e. the same game system id as the frozen `.gst` (revision 8), no `catalogueLink`, so it is self-contained in this fixture set.
- The four files already in `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` all differ byte-wise from upstream head, so the README's "two vintages" statement is factual.
- Parsed into the corpus, the book adds exactly ONE new cell: `repeat|selectionCount|parent|child=upgrade|repeats=1|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|roundUp=false|pct=false`, 3 occurrences (the three `childId="upgrade"` repeats; `childId` keyword `upgrade` is documented in `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` §7.7's attribute table). Every other construct it carries falls into a cell the corpus already holds. It produces no `parsererror`.
- Corpus totals move 105 -> 106 cells, covered stays 105, uncovered 0 -> 1.

STEP 1 — copy the file verbatim. From the repo root:
  `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/artkoenig/Warhammer-Fantasy-6th-edition /tmp/whfb6-upstream`
  `git -C /tmp/whfb6-upstream rev-parse HEAD`  (must print `9c7203c94221a4a98d5c1ffcfcfaedafe7d6d233`; if it does not, clone without `--depth` and `git -C /tmp/whfb6-upstream checkout 9c7203c94221a4a98d5c1ffcfcfaedafe7d6d233`)
  `cp "/tmp/whfb6-upstream/Dogs of War.cat" "src/__fixtures__/whfb6/Dogs of War.cat"`
Verify with the sha256 check listed in `checks`. Do not reformat, re-indent or normalise the file in any way, and do not touch the other four files in that directory.

STEP 2 — `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/README.md`. The file is German prose; leave the existing German text untouched and add the new material in English (repo convention for new text, cf. `scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md`). Extend the `## Herkunft` section and add one short section so the README states, explicitly:
- `Dogs of War.cat` was copied verbatim from `artkoenig/Warhammer-Fantasy-6th-edition` at commit `9c7203c94221a4a98d5c1ffcfcfaedafe7d6d233`, the current upstream head.
- The other four files come from commit `d13b7e5` and predate the whitespace cleanup of issue 11 (commit `db7848d`), so the directory now deliberately carries TWO vintages: one book at upstream head, the rest in the older, uncleaned form whose leading/trailing whitespace the E2E is meant to run through.
- Why this book is here (issue 0148): it carries rule constructs no other book of this set carries — the only `childId="upgrade"` repeats in either fixture corpus (3 occurrences), i.e. the cell `repeat|selectionCount|parent|child=upgrade|repeats=1|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|roundUp=false|pct=false`, which is unreachable for the evaluator coverage campaign without it.
Keep the existing `## Update-Politik` promise intact — this addition IS such a functional reason and can be named as one.

STEP 3 — regenerate `docs/testing/worklist.json`. Run `node scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js`. Its exit code is now 1, not 0, and that is the documented normal outcome for a non-empty worklist (see the script's header comment); it is not a check command and its exit code judges nothing here. The regenerated file must read `"totals": { "cells": 106, "covered": 105, "uncovered": 1 }` and carry exactly one entry in `cells`, the `child=upgrade` repeat cell above, with `"src/__fixtures__/whfb6/Dogs of War.cat": 3` in its `files` map. The `corpus` array does not change: `CORPUS_DIRS` in `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.js` fixes the corpus by directory, so nothing in the library needs an edit. Commit the regenerated file. Change nothing else under `docs/testing/` — `covered-cells.json` and `campaign-state.json` stay as they are (I checked: no key in `covered-cells.json` is revived by the added book, and the stale-key warning list stays empty).

STEP 4 — app E2E. `scripts/lib/e2e-harness.js` zips every `.cat`/`.gst` of `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/`, so the app under test now imports 5 files instead of 4 (+304 KB on ~1.3 MB). What I checked and what it means:
- `e2e/ui.test.js` picks the catalogue by option text containing `Ogre Kingdoms` and falls back to `selectedIndex = 1` only if that is missing, so the extra book does not change which army it builds. No assertion in it counts catalogues, units or options absolutely.
- `scripts/lib/e2e-harness.test.js` asserts only that the directory contains `Warhammer Fantasy Battle 6th edition.gst` and that every collected name ends in `.cat`/`.gst`. Both still hold; no edit needed.
- No other test reads the fixture directory by listing it — every one of the ten `src/**` tests that touch `src/__fixtures__/whfb6` names its files explicitly (verified by grepping `readdirSync` across `src/`). `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js` resolves scenario datasets by explicit path and no scenario names Dogs of War, so it does not see the book either.
- The one real risk is time: `SYSTEM_IMPORT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` in `scripts/lib/e2e-harness.js` bounds the upload-and-parse wait. If the E2E now fails waiting for `.desktop-nav-actions`, raise that constant (and only that) in the harness — that is the sanctioned fix. Never solve E2E fallout by leaving the book out of the fixture directory or by filtering it out of the zip.

STEP 5 — screenshot. Run `node scripts/generate_screenshots.js` (offline, no catalog data needed) and use `.screenshots/desktop_02_bibliothekar_loaded.png` for the pull request: that is the library view listing the imported catalogues, and it is the view whose content demonstrably changes through the added book. Note that the same script picks the FIRST catalogue in the roster dialog (`selectedIndex = 1`), which is now most likely `Dogs of War` instead of `Ogre Kingdoms`, so screenshots 04-08 will show a different army; that is cosmetic and expected. If the script throws at `clickRequired('.category-unit-adder-container button')` because the Dogs of War army renders no primary category group, that is a screenshot-tooling problem, not an app bug — capture 01/02 by cutting the run short there rather than changing app code, and report it.

EXPLICITLY NOT PART OF THIS INCREMENT:
- Do NOT raise the `beforeAll` hook timeout in `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js`. That criterion exists because 17 files blow past vitest's 10-second default; at 10 files the hook parses ~10% more than today's ~2s and stays well inside it. Increment 2 raises it.
- Do NOT add any definitive book, do NOT touch `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` or its README, and do NOT re-baseline the inventory to the 17-file / 130-cell numbers of the issue.
- No production code under `src/` changes. No version bump (test fixtures change nothing a user can see; the issue decides this too).

return.testPlan:
WHETHER: tests are needed. Not new behaviour — the corpus drift guard `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js` is written for a nine-file corpus and its baselines have to be re-baselined to the ten-file one, plus one new case that pins why the book is in the repository at all.

HOW I RECOMPUTED THE BASELINES (so they can be re-derived, not trusted): I cloned the upstream repo into the scratchpad, copied the four current `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/` files plus `Dogs of War.cat` into a temp directory, and ran a throwaway node script from the repo root that calls `loadCorpus([WHFB6_DEFINITIVE_DIR, tempDir])` and `extractCells` from the real library and diffs the result against `loadCorpus([WHFB6_DEFINITIVE_DIR, WHFB6_DIR])`. That was the one measurement I ran, and I ran it because every baseline below depends on it; it is not a check command and no test was executed. The per-kind totals below are independently confirmed by the `grep -rhoE '<tag[ />]' | wc -l` arbiter: today's corpus greps to exactly the numbers the file already asserts, and `Dogs of War.cat` alone greps to constraint 362, condition 52, conditionGroup 0, modifier 80, modifierGroup 0, repeat 30, repeats 30.

WHAT — per criterion, all in `scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js` (vitest, jsdom environment, `DOMParser` is a global; conventions live in `scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md`, load it):

1. Criterion "the corpus test passes with recomputed baselines":
   a. Case 21 (`loadCorpus — static walk of both fixture sets`): `corpus.sources` length 9 -> 10; the definitive slice stays 5; the other slice 4 -> 5. `corpus.failures` stays `[]` (the added file parses clean) and the README-exclusion assertion is unchanged. Update the `it` title, which says "exactly nine".
   b. Case 22 (per-kind occurrence totals): constraint 5290 -> 5652, condition 1739 -> 1791, conditionGroup 261 (unchanged), modifier 1762 -> 1842, modifierGroup 121 (unchanged), repeat 214 -> 244, repeatList 213 -> 243. Keep the comment block that names the grep as arbiter and extend it to say the totals were recomputed for the ten-file corpus in issue 0148.
   c. Case 23 (landmark cells): NO CHANGE. `conditionGroup|not|nested` stays at 2 occurrences (Dogs of War has no `conditionGroup` at all), the first `condition|greaterThanOrEqualTo|...` cell stays `condition|greaterThanOrEqualTo|parent|selectionCount|child=id` with 1 occurrence (no `greaterThanOrEqualTo` in the added book), the `modifier|...|unresolvedTarget` cell is still found (`modifier|decrement|unresolvedTarget`), and all seven kinds are still present. Verify, do not edit.
   d. Cases 24-26 (worklist drift guard): the deep-equal against the committed `docs/testing/worklist.json` needs no code change but only passes once the implementer has regenerated that file — if it fails with an empty `cells` array on the committed side, the regeneration step has not landed yet. The explicit totals assertion moves from `{ cells: 105, covered: 105, uncovered: 0 }` to `{ cells: 106, covered: 105, uncovered: 1 }`, and its comment gets one line: the single added cell is `repeat|selectionCount|parent|child=upgrade|repeats=1|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|roundUp=false|pct=false`, uncovered by design (closing it is the campaign's work, out of scope for issue 0148). The internal-consistency case and the ordering case need no change.
   e. Cases B1/B2 (duplicated id `1077-7379-f142-f382`): NO CHANGE. The id does not occur in Dogs of War; the roster-scope cell keeps 1 occurrence and the `files` map `{ 'src/__fixtures__/whfb6/Warhammer Fantasy Battle 6th edition.gst': 1 }`. Verify, do not edit.
   f. Case B4 (covered/uncovered partition): NO CHANGE — it asserts a relation, not a number.
   g. Case B5 (unmatched resolution failures): NO CHANGE. `outside-dataset` stays empty and the six-id `unknown-id` set stays as it is — I grepped Dogs of War for all four real ids (`02cd-cabf-7e25-2b09`, `d96c-c95f-8224-7c87`, `ce6e-afde-2ed1-aac2`, `a59d-2ddb-429c-1aca`): none occurs, so no id can flip from unknown to outside-dataset. Verify, do not edit.
   h. Case R7 (distinct `repeat|` cells): 11 -> 12.
   i. Case R8 (landmark flagged repeat cells): NO CHANGE, 16 and 12. Both landmarks carry `ics=true`/scope `roster`, while all 30 repeats of Dogs of War are scope `parent` with `includeChildSelections="false"`. Verify, do not edit.
   j. Cases 29-34 (`loadCoverageRecords` temp-directory failure paths): NO CHANGE.
   k. Do NOT raise the `beforeAll` hook timeout. Ten files stay far inside vitest's 10-second default; that edit belongs to the increment that adds seven more books.

2. Criterion "the book carries rule constructs no other book of its set carries" — ADD ONE CASE to the same file, next to R7/R8, at integration level: the corpus holds the cell `repeat|selectionCount|parent|child=upgrade|repeats=1|s=true|ics=false|icf=false|roundUp=false|pct=false` with 3 occurrences, and its `files` map is exactly `{ 'src/__fixtures__/whfb6/Dogs of War.cat': 3 }`. That single assertion is what makes "this book and no other reaches this construct" checkable, and it fails loudly if the book is ever removed or replaced by a different vintage.

3. Criterion "byte-identical to upstream" and "the four existing files unchanged": NOT covered by a test. A committed sha256 in a test file would be a maintenance burden with no reader, and the repo has no such convention. The two shell commands in `checks` judge both facts exactly and cost nothing.

4. Criteria "npm test passes" and "a screenshot is produced": covered by the check commands, not by new cases. No new E2E assertion is asked for — the app E2E's job here is to prove the enlarged fixture still imports, not to test the added book.

SUITE DOC: `scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md` is present and its conventions match what I read in the test file, with one contradiction the test-author has to correct as part of its step: the paragraph on the character-class grep quotes measurements from the nine-file corpus and says "`repeats` reads 0 instead of 213". With the tenth file that number is 243. Update that one figure (the `modifierGroup` 121/109 figures stay correct) and leave the rest of the doc alone.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE: the closed list in `checks`, run from the repository root, nothing else.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED: I ran none of the check commands, not even as a baseline. Predicted from reading: on the current tree everything is green; the moment `Dogs of War.cat` lands, `npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js` goes red on cases 21, 22, 24 and R7 and on the worklist deep-equal until both the re-baselined test file and the regenerated `docs/testing/worklist.json` are in place. If the test-author runs before the implementer, that red is expected and the numbers above are written for the post-copy corpus.

return.summary: Increment 1 accepted with no findings. All four listed commands run from the repository root, chained in one call: the sha256 check on src/__fixtures__/whfb6/Dogs of War.cat exit 0 (OK); git diff --exit-code against claude/evaluator-ergofang-daten-ni8js9 over the three older catalogues and the .gst exit 0 (no byte moved); npx vitest run scripts/lib/evaluator-coverage-corpus.test.js exit 0 (29 cases, one file, 6.7s, nothing skipped); npm test exit 0 (full vitest run plus the puppeteer app E2E, which imported the enlarged fixture and passed every UI assertion). Two probes, both from a stated doubt. Probe 1 — doubt: are case 22's moved baselines recomputed from the corpus or nudged until green? I re-ran the character-class grep the test file itself names as arbiter (grep -rhoE '<tag[ />]' over both fixture dirs): constraint 5652, condition 1791, conditionGroup 261, modifier 1842, modifierGroup 121, repeat 244, repeats 243 — every asserted number matches exactly, including the two that deliberately did not move, and the corrected figure in scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md (repeats 243, modifierGroup still 109 under the trailing-space form). grep -rc 'childId="upgrade"' over both fixture directories returns Dogs of War.cat: 3 and nothing else, so the README's uniqueness claim and the new case 35 both hold. Probe 2 — doubt: is the file really byte-identical to upstream, or only to the hash the prompt carries? I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/artkoenig/Warhammer-Fantasy-6th-edition/9c7203c94221a4a98d5c1ffcfcfaedafe7d6d233/Dogs%20of%20War.cat into the scratchpad (HTTP 200) and hashed it: 90211630f9fdf6169289fe6a98d6ab84c521cc38644d2c24ca9f720a285a9e66, identical to the committed file. The GitHub API is blocked for that repo in this session (HTTP 403), so 'current upstream head' in the README is stated but not independently confirmed; the criterion only asks that the README state it. Criterion by criterion: the fixture file is verbatim upstream (probe 2); the four older files are untouched (listed command 2); README.md carries the provenance of the added book, a 'Two vintages on purpose' section naming both vintages and why they must not be harmonised, and a 'Warum Dogs of War' section naming the childId=upgrade cell (probe 1 confirms the claim is true); the corpus test passes with baselines that survive the grep arbiter; npm test is green with no change to the app E2E or its harness, which globs every .cat/.gst of the fixture directory and therefore ships the book without an edit; and .screenshots/desktop_02_bibliothekar_loaded.png shows the library view reading '4 faction catalogues loaded' where it read 3 before the book, i.e. a view whose content the added book changed. Blast radius traced, nothing found: scripts/lib/e2e-harness.js and e2e/ui.test.js select by name and by extension, never by count or index; src/utils/rosterSerialization.integration.test.js names its three catalogues explicitly and does not list the directory; the README's 'Kleinste der drei WHFB6-Kataloge' sentence is scoped to the three catalogues used in that test and stays true (Ogre Kingdoms 206 KB is also still smaller than Dogs of War 304 KB); no ADR or doc outside the diff states a file count for this fixture directory. Two files in the diff no criterion names, both justified rather than scope creep: docs/testing/worklist.json (106/105/1 with the one uncovered child=upgrade cell) is what the drift guard deep-equals against, so criterion 4 cannot pass without it, and the one figure in scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md would be false without its correction. Observations that cost the run nothing: the new README sections are English inside an otherwise German document, and .screenshots/ is gitignored, so the screenshot cannot ride in the diff — whoever opens the pull request has to attach /home/user/tome_of_battle/.screenshots/desktop_02_bibliothekar_loaded.png by hand. One disclosure: a broad grep over docs/ for stale corpus counts incidentally printed lines of the increment's backlog.json into my context; I based no part of this review on them, and every fact above rests on a command or probe I ran myself.
